content: The administration of uterotonic drugs is a critical component of active management during the third stage of labor. The timing of administering these drugs varies globally and may have significant effects on maternal and neonatal health. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of administering prophylactic uterotonics either before or after placental delivery on outcomes related to the third stage of labor. The research involved a systematic review of randomized controlled trials. Three trials, including a total of 1,671 participants, were analyzed. Oxytocin was the only uterotonic drug used in these studies, with variations in its dosage and route of administration. The findings revealed that the timing of oxytocin administration—whether before or after placental expulsion—did not significantly affect several key clinical outcomes. Specifically, the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage (defined as blood loss greater than 500 mL) was not significantly different between the two timing groups (risk ratio [RR] 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62 to 1.04). Similarly, the rate of retained placenta (RR 1.54, 95% CI 0.76 to 3.11) and the duration of the third stage of labor (mean difference [MD] -0.30 minutes, 95% CI -0.95 to 0.36) were not significantly influenced by the timing of oxytocin administration. Other outcomes, such as total postpartum blood loss (MD 22.32 mL, 95% CI -58.21 to 102.86), changes in maternal hemoglobin levels (MD 0.06 g/dL, 95% CI -0.60 to 0.72), and the need for blood transfusion (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.23 to 2.73), also showed no significant differences. Additionally, the use of additional uterotonics (RR 1.10, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.52), the incidence of maternal hypotension (RR 2.48, 95% CI 0.23 to 26.70), and the occurrence of severe postpartum hemorrhage (defined as blood loss of 1,000 mL or more; RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.98) were not significantly affected by the timing of oxytocin administration. It is important to note that no data were available on other maternal or neonatal outcomes. The authors concluded that the timing of oxytocin administration, whether before or after placental expulsion, does not significantly influence many clinically important outcomes, such as postpartum hemorrhage, placental retention, or the duration of the third stage of labor. However, the number of studies included in this analysis was limited, and oxytocin was the only uterotonic drug evaluated, primarily administered via intravenous infusion. Therefore, caution is advised when extrapolating these findings to other routes of administration or other uterotonic drugs. Further research is needed to assess additional maternal and neonatal outcomes using standardized methodologies.
